verdict.summary: User OAuth (identify, guilds, email) and bot installs are self-serve with no review, and since June 10, 2026 privileged intents like MESSAGE_CONTENT only need review once a bot can reach 10,000 users. The catches are the 100-server cap for unverified bots (App Verification needs team-owner identity verification) and a set of partner-only scopes such as dm_channels.read and rpc.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create an application, add a redirect URI, copy client ID/secret, and run the code flow or bot invite link. No review for development.

timeToProd.assumes: A bot that reads messages (bot scope + MESSAGE_CONTENT intent) and grows past 100 servers, which needs App Verification; a bot in under 100 servers and under 10,000 users, or user-only OAuth, is live the same day.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Nothing for user OAuth or small bots. For growth: App Verification (team-owner identity verification) before the 100th server, and a privileged intent application within 90 days of crossing 10,000 users.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Thresholds are sourced; Discord publishes no review durations, so the upper bound is our estimate.

prerequisites.item: A Discord account (ideally with 2FA) and a Developer Team for the app
prerequisites.why: Apps are created in the Developer Portal; App Verification requires the team owner to complete identity verification, and bots with elevated permissions need 2FA on the owner account for 2FA-enforced servers.

prerequisites.item: A registered redirect URI matching the one sent in authorize and token requests
prerequisites.why: redirect_uri must be one registered on the app and must match in the token exchange.

prerequisites.item: A clear data-handling story (storage, retention, security) for any privileged intent
prerequisites.why: Privileged intent applications are judged on a specific use case and on how data is stored, retained and secured.

scopeTiers.impact: Sign-in and knowing which servers a user is in. Self-serve for any user.
Bot can post, run slash commands and read message events that mention it. Unverified apps are limited to 100 servers; verification is required beyond that.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 100-guild verification requirement is stated in the gateway docs.

scopeTiers.impact: Needed for an agent that reads message text in channels. Toggle-on under 10,000 reachable users; above that, apply within 90 days and reapply every year.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: reviewRequired=false describes the small-app path; large apps need review.

scopeTiers.impact: Reading a user's DMs or controlling their client needs approved-partner status; activities.read/write are not available to apps. Requesting them without approval may cause errors in the OAuth flow.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: messages.read is an RPC scope; that it's effectively partner-only is our reading of the rpc restrictions.

steps.title: Create the application
steps.detail: In the Developer Portal, click New Application (ideally under a Team so verification and ownership are shared). Copy the client ID and reset/copy the client secret.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The portal URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20; we did not sign in.

steps.title: Decide user OAuth vs bot
steps.detail: User OAuth (identify guilds) acts as the user with limited read scopes; reading channel messages for an agent means a bot plus the MESSAGE_CONTENT intent. Check 'You Might Not Need a Privileged Intent' first (slash commands and mentions don't need it).

steps.title: Configure OAuth2 redirects and the bot user
steps.detail: Add redirect URIs under OAuth2, create the bot under Bot, and toggle needed privileged intents (allowed freely under 10,000 users).

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow with PKCE
steps.detail: Redirect to https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&scope=identify%20guilds%20bot&permissions=...&redirect_uri=...&state=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256. Exchange at POST https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token (form-encoded only). Read guild_id from the redirect as a hint. Validate the new iss parameter.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: S256 PKCE support observed in the OIDC discovery document.

steps.title: Add refresh and revocation handling
steps.detail: Example tokens expire in 604800 s (7 days); refresh with grant_type=refresh_token. Treat invalid_grant like an APPLICATION_DEAUTHORIZED event and prompt reconnect.

steps.title: Build rate-limit handling
steps.detail: Respect per-route buckets and the 50 req/s global limit, honour 429 retry_after, and keep invalid (401/403/429) responses well under 10,000 per 10 minutes to avoid Cloudflare IP bans.

steps.title: Launch to users (no review)
steps.detail: Share the install/authorize link. Any user or server admin can connect immediately.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: No review step exists in the OAuth docs for non-restricted scopes.

steps.title: Prepare App Verification before 100 servers
steps.detail: Draft the privacy policy, terms of service and app description the verification checklist asks for; check the portal's App Verification page for the current criteria.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The exact checklist is only shown inside the portal; privacy policy/ToS as items are our expectation.

steps.title: Complete team-owner identity verification and submit
steps.detail: The team owner completes identity verification, then submits the app for verification from the App Verification page.

steps.title: Wait for App Verification
steps.detail: Discord reviews the app; verification also unlocks Discovery and monetization.

steps.title: Apply for privileged intents at 10,000 users
steps.detail: When the portal notifies you that the app reaches 10,000 users, submit a specific use-case and data-handling description within 90 days. Reapply yearly. The app can keep joining servers during review.

agentCanDo: Choose scopes, bot permissions integer and intents (and check whether a privileged intent is avoidable)
Implement the code flow with PKCE, iss validation, refresh and revocation
Build rate-limit and 429 handling that avoids Cloudflare invalid-request bans
Draft privacy policy, ToS and the privileged-intent use-case and data-handling write-up
Verify endpoints via the OIDC and OAuth metadata documents
humanMustDo: Sign in to the Developer Portal, create the app and bot, and store the secret
Toggle privileged intents and register redirect URIs
Complete team-owner identity verification and submit App Verification
Submit the privileged intent application (and yearly reapplication) when notified
Customer side: a server admin with Manage Server authorizes the bot

blockers.symptom: Gateway connection closes with code 4014 (Disallowed intent)
blockers.cause: The bot passed a privileged intent (e.g. MESSAGE_CONTENT) that isn't enabled or approved for the app.
blockers.fix: Toggle the intent in the portal (under 10,000 users) or get it approved in review.

blockers.symptom: Bot receives messages with empty content fields
blockers.cause: Without the MESSAGE_CONTENT intent, content is only present in some cases such as messages that mention the bot or DMs.
blockers.fix: Enable MESSAGE_CONTENT, or redesign around slash commands and mentions.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Exceptions are described in the message content intent docs section, which we read only partially.

blockers.symptom: Bot can't be added to more servers at around 100 guilds
blockers.cause: Unverified apps are limited to 100 servers.
blockers.fix: Submit App Verification (team-owner identity verification) before hitting the cap.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The gateway docs say verification is required for 100+ guilds; the exact error behaviour comes from community posts.

blockers.symptom: OAuth errors or odd behaviour when requesting scopes like dm_channels.read or rpc
blockers.cause: These scopes are limited to approved partners.
blockers.fix: Remove them; use a bot with channel access instead of reading users' DMs.

blockers.symptom: Repeated temporary bans / Cloudflare 1015-style blocks from the Discord API
blockers.cause: More than 10,000 invalid (401/403/429) requests in 10 minutes from one IP.
blockers.fix: Stop retrying on 401/403, honour retry_after, and log invalid-request rate.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The Cloudflare error number is our addition, not from the docs.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails with a content-type error
blockers.cause: The token and revoke endpoints only accept application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

nuances.text: Since June 10, 2026 the privileged intent threshold is 10,000 reachable users (not 100 servers), access must be reconfirmed every year, and App Verification is a separate process from intent review. Many third-party guides still describe the old 100-server intent rule.
Access tokens in Discord's examples last 7 days (expires_in 604800) with a refresh token. Revoking one token revokes all tokens for that authorization.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The docs show this as an example value, not a guaranteed policy.

nuances.text: Bots get 50 requests/second globally plus per-route limits; increases are requested through support (dis.gd/rate-limit).
Discord's policy-update FAQ says it does not allow AI companies to train models on users' messages, which matters for any agent that stores message content.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: This is Discord's general policy FAQ; we couldn't open the Developer Policy itself (HTTP 403).

nuances.text: Since October 14, 2026 authorization redirects include iss=https://discord.com (RFC 9207); clients can validate it to prevent mix-up attacks.
Discord is also an OIDC provider (issuer https://discord.com, S256 PKCE, RS256 ID tokens).
Developer docs moved to docs.discord.com (Mintlify) in 2026; old discord.com/developers/docs URLs 301-redirect there, and there's a docs MCP server at docs.discord.com/mcp.
